summary: Backend-only verification of the LLM language-enforcement bug fix on POST /api/chat/stream. All 8 tests PASSED (100% success rate) against the live preview backend using protest@gandhikar.in on basic mode (samples untouched). Confirmed: (1) Tamil / Hindi / Bengali replies now come back FULLY translated — section headings, bullets AND disclaimer are all rendered in the target script (>=30 script chars each), (2) the English literals 'Answer:' and 'What you can do:' do NOT appear in the first 120 chars of any non-English reply, (3) English selection still emits English 'Answer:' / 'What you can do:' headings unchanged, (4) backwards compatibility: omitting `language_native` from the request body still produces a fully-Tamil reply because the backend derives native from the LANGUAGES table, (5) sanitize_model_output correctly strips markdown ** bolds — no ** leaks in any assembled body, (6) citation SSE frames still fire and precede the first delta frame for a Tamil query on the arrest-rights topic (English keyword retrieval works regardless of UI language).
action_items: No fixes required — language enforcement bug is resolved. Main agent may proceed to next task.
critical_code_review_comments: build_system_prompt @ server.py:174-268 correctly composes `lang_display = 'Tamil (தமிழ்)'` and injects a shouted REPLY LANGUAGE rule + explicit label_hint that instructs the model to translate the section headings (was previously biased by the English literals in the FORMAT block).
The FORMAT block @ server.py:247-258 now uses placeholder syntax `<heading meaning "Answer:" in Tamil (தமிழ்)>` instead of the raw English tokens, which was the root cause of the leak.
Endpoint @ server.py:539-544 correctly derives `lang_native` from the LANGUAGES table when the client omits `language_native` — backward compatibility path validated end-to-end.
SSE ordering @ server.py:611-657: session frame first, then all citation frames, then LLM deltas, then optional final (sanitized) frame, then done. Verified in Tamil citations test.
sanitize_model_output final-frame path @ server.py:652-655 ensures the client sees the cleaned text; no ** leaked in any of the four language runs.
seed_data_creation: None. Reused existing free-tier user protest@gandhikar.in in BASIC mode so no pro samples were consumed.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Language enforcement fix is verified. Tests live at /app/backend/tests/test_language_enforcement.py — reuse as a regression suite. Each language run takes ~10-15s (real Claude Sonnet 4.5 stream). Total suite runtime ~67s. Uses BASIC mode so no paywall interaction; the fix applies equally to PRO mode because build_system_prompt language rules run for both. Script-range regex constants: Tamil U+0B80-U+0BFF, Devanagari U+0900-U+097F, Bengali U+0980-U+09FF. English-heading-literal-leak guard uses first 120 chars of the assembled body.
rca_of_issue: Original bug: prompt said 'REPLY LANGUAGE: Tamil' but the FORMAT block listed the two section labels as raw English strings ('Answer:', 'What you can do:'), so the model copied them literally into non-English replies while only translating the trailing disclaimer. Fix: (a) add language_native to ChatIn + auto-derive from LANGUAGES table for backward compat, (b) prompt now uses `Tamil (தமிழ்)` display form, (c) explicit label_hint tells the model the headings MUST be in the target language, (d) FORMAT placeholders now describe the headings semantically (`<heading meaning "Answer:" in Tamil (தமிழ்)>`) instead of embedding the English token. All three targeted languages (ta/hi/bn) now return full-body translations end-to-end via /api/chat/stream.
